text:
on "the eminent dead," Lyndon Johnson, power dynamics, respect, cunning, and manipulative behavior

"dead men tell no tales"

1/9

reason #1000 why u want to study the eminent dead, is because a lot of the most useful information as far as navigating society, politics, and "the ways of men"... is stuff that people will never admit to doing, for fear of being perceived as manipulative or cunning.

as always, the truth is nuanced...

when u study the past 2000 years of biography, history etc, u will see that men are the same in all eras

but then in real life, u will sometimes hit a divergence

"why doesn't this person fit the fact pattern that I know"

it's because they're on some straight-up bullshit lol

faking like turkey bacon

it's not always nefarious, sometimes men are forced by circumstance into a persona that just isn't them -- living a lie for years on end -- but as I will explain, this is why u have to study the dead ones.

over and over, people u know will reveal that they weren't who they seemed to be...and as a result, u have a head full of incorrect conclusions that u drew based on some Potemkin personality type.

2.

a few of the eminent dead who come to mind, there are men like LBJ who absolutely fit these adjectives (manipulative, deceitful, cunning) by nature, unapologetically so.

or Ben Franklin, or Talleyrand, pretty much any diplomat or politician who made it to the #1 seed, u can guarantee they're wired that way more than most.

but every single man is born with these traits in them, just to varying degrees.

think of any corporate setting you've ever been in, as a fly on the wall, watching human beings do what they do, and ask "how much of this is manipulative behavior"

all the sucking up and brown nosing, trying to appear to ppl a certain way

always thinking "I want to say X but I can't, so I'll say Y"

if it isn't the truth, there is manipulation involved

"white lies," all the hierarchy/power structure considerations, the way that you treat the CEO different than you treat a summer intern

this is all manipulative behavior even if u prefer to call it something nicer.

3.

the way people treat the intern is usually their true nature

which means the way u see them treating the CEO, or their boss... is almost entirely bullshit, manipulation, and cunning.

an honest man will be open about "I have engaged in this behavior," a dishonest man will say "everyone else does that stuff, except for me."

this tends to be a universal truth, and out of 100 ppl, may reveal the 2 or 3 who aren't completely full of shit.

additionally, it is almost impossible to know others, to know human nature, to know the ways of men and all their vices, while also lying to yourself about whether these same vices exist within you (hint: they do).

4.

either way, the goal here is to thread the needle

that means, first and foremost, becoming fluent in how all this shit works...all the social dynamics, from respect to power, so that u can "read the room" no matter where u are.

and then second, trying to embody all the positive traits that will get u what u want -- meaning u get rid of all "fake it til u make it," u consciously choose not to engage in any manipulative or cunning behavior, or anything that could even be perceived as such.

every action has both a selfless and a selfish motive

its good to acknowledge both, not just internally, but in dealing w/ others and putting all ur cards on the table

because when u hear a man claim he's driven by 100% pure altruism... 🚩🚩🚩

people are driven far more by selfish motives than selfless ones

this is just basic human nature, and it's the origin of Franklin's "appeal to interest and not to reason." Munger writes about this ad nauseum in the context of wrongdoing at Salomon Brothers.

5.

but here, the selfless motive of not "faking it til u make it" is that this is just a mark of good character, u are the same person 24/7.

at the same time, the selfish motive is that all manipulation and cunning will be detected by the people at the top (the #1 seed, CEO, whoever)

u dont get there and stay there unless u can read people.

from the outside, u will see others trying to "run game" on them, and while they appear to be falling for it, they operate on 3rd or 4th level thinking

i.e. "I'm going to let this person think they're manipulating me"

the gameplan being...bait them, let them drop their guard, and then let them overplay their hand.

now, they'll never admit to you, or to any other living soul, that this is how they operate. 

for two reasons.

first, to reveal the web would result in never catching another fly. this is the selfish motive.

second, as in the intro, this is the type of behavior that would be deemed manipulative, cunning, and perhaps shameful.

no living man wants to be known as those things, thus, he will deny it or lie about it until the day he dies

and this is yet another reason why you have to study dead men to learn the truth.

if u didn't understand what I meant at the start of this post, I think u should by now.

6.

point being, u can assume that the person who you want/need to like you...the one who is higher up...is someone that spends their entire day dealing with people who are 1000x better at bullshit, manipulation, and cunning than u are.

once again, the best way to win the game is to not play it at all.

so for me to say, "you should figure out who you need to like you, and then make them like you," would be horrible advice bc it's self-defeating.

they will see exactly what u are trying to do and it will backfire, because they will sense that you aren't being genuine in your intent.

7.

this is what I mean by thread the needle.

you probably want to be able to enter a room and understand, intuitively, who is respected and who isn't -- which u can learn from studying the Lyndon Johnson types

but beyond that, the middle ground isn't "what can I say to someone that will make them respect me"

it's, how can I be someone that they will naturally end up respecting?

and this tends to be the opposite route.

8.

they're going to be most curious about the person who is clearly courteous and respectful, but who isn't flattering them or treating them any different than they treat the summer intern.

this process, them viewing u as different from the rest, can only occur gradually, organically, and over long periods of time.

the other ppl thinking, "what 1x thing can I say/do to make them like me" -- this always fails.

some of the positive can be gained simply thru years of not engaging in the negative

but if I really had to put words to it, I'd phrase it as: "integrity has a way of leaking out."

9.

they're going to learn who u really are not thru direct observation, but from the 1000's of pieces of info they hear from others about their 1x1 interactions with u, behind closed doors.

honestly, someone high up will get the best read from talking to the summer intern

i.e. "who do you like here"

"oh, I like so-and-so the best, he spends a ton of time going out of his way to teach me shit, help me learn and answer my questions"

no one has anything to gain from the guy at the very bottom

and so thats why this guy provides a clearer read on someone's character, than the version that he sees each day presented to his face.

END/SUMMARY

this is not really an advice post, or one where I can guide u...as I said before, anything forced will be sensed as such, and the correct path is specific to who u are.

the operative Q to answer, is from the view of a fly on the wall: "if you were someone else, would you admire and respect you?"

and the best path to that is some mix of, "be genuine in ur intent" and "have a high degree of earned self-respect."

but to my knowledge, there is no way to achieve those things other than to be authentically yourself -- whoever that person may be.

everything else will fail.

the closest thing to a universal truth that u will find, directly observable in the ways of men, can be found in this quote by Samuel Johnson, and in my experience it has proved 100% accurate and reliable:

"The true measure of a man is how he treats someone who can do him absolutely no good."
